questions.question: When was ISRO founded?
questions.source_sentence: It was founded on 15 August 1969 under the leadership of Vikram Sarabhai, who is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.

questions.question: Where is ISRO headquartered?
questions.source_sentence: ISRO is headquartered in Bengaluru and works under the Department of Space, which reports directly to the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In February 2017 a single PSLV mission carried a record ______ satellites into orbit.
questions.source_sentence: In February 2017 a single PSLV mission carried a record 104 satellites into orbit.

questions.question: True or False: Its Indian Space Research Organisation, helped confirm the presence of water molecules on the lunar surface.
questions.source_sentence: Its Moon Impact Probe helped confirm the presence of water molecules on the lunar surface.

questions.question: When did India land a spacecraft near the south pole of the Moon?
questions.source_sentence: On 23 August 2023, Chandrayaan-3 made India the first nation to land a spacecraft near the south pole of the Moon.

questions.question: What did ISRO launch Aditya-L1 to study?
questions.source_sentence: A few days later, on 2 September 2023, ISRO launched Aditya-L1, its first mission to study the Sun from the first Lagrange point.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: ISRO's heavy-lift rocket, ______ will carry the Gaganyaan capsule, which is intended to take Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit.
questions.source_sentence: ISRO's heavy-lift rocket, the LVM3, will carry the Gaganyaan capsule, which is intended to take Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit.

questions.question: True or False: ISRO also serves everyday needs.
